c.tagline: Bavarian wine city crowned by a UNESCO prince-bishops' Residence and the Old Main Bridge

taxi.fareNote: Traditional cream-colored taxis operate metered fares regulated by the city; ranks are at the Hauptbahnhof and Marktplatz

emergency.note: 110 reaches police, 112 reaches fire and ambulance services; both are toll-free nationwide

hood_desc: The compact historic core packed with the Würzburg Residence, Marienberg Fortress views, and the Old Main Bridge lined with wine stands. Almost everything worth seeing is within walking distance here.
A riverside district across the Main, overlooked by the Käppele pilgrimage church on its hillside vineyards. Quieter and residential, with easy footpaths up to panoramic viewpoints.
A leafy residential quarter south of downtown bordering the Ringpark, popular with families and known for tidy streets and small local shops.
Home to the University of Würzburg's main campus, giving the area a young, café-and-bar energy with a steady student population.
A working-class district around the main train station, convenient for arrivals and offering some of the city's better-value accommodation.

water.note: German tap water is strictly regulated and safe to drink.

transit.pay: VVM zone tickets from machines, app, or onboard; day passes available
transit.note: Compact tram-and-bus network makes most sights reachable without a car; the Altstadt itself is pedestrian-friendly

train: Würzburg Hauptbahnhof is a major ICE hub on the Frankfurt-Nuremberg-Munich line, ~1h15 to Frankfurt
bus: Regional buses and the Romantic Road coach route

car.idp: Not required for EU visitors, recommended for others

tip.r: Round up or add roughly 5-10%, stating the total aloud when paying rather than leaving cash on the table

food.name: Meefischli
food.desc: Tiny whole fish from the river Main, floured and deep-fried crisp, eaten head, tail and all with lemon and a glass of Silvaner. Pure Wuerzburg.

places.name: Backoefele
places.note: Warren of wood-panelled rooms in a 17th-century house; the classic address for Meefischli.

places.name: Alte Mainmuehle
places.note: Old mill on the river beside the bridge; fried Main fish with a fortress view.

places.name: Weinhaus zum Stachel
places.note: Wuerzburg's oldest wine tavern, in a vine-covered courtyard dating to 1413.

food.name: Blaue Zipfel
food.desc: Raw bratwurst poached in a tart vinegar broth with onion, bay and peppercorns until the skins turn blue-grey. Sour, light and utterly Franconian.

places.name: Backoefele
places.note: Serves the full Franconian canon; Blaue Zipfel arrive in the broth in a deep bowl.

places.name: Buergerspital Weinstuben
places.note: Tavern of a charitable wine estate founded in 1316; regional cooking with its own wines.

places.name: Ratskeller Wuerzburg
places.note: Vaulted cellar under the old town hall, dependable for Franconian sausage dishes.

food.name: Fraenkische Bratwurst
food.desc: Coarse, marjoram-scented Franconian bratwurst, grilled over beechwood and served with sauerkraut and dark bread rather than in a bun.

places.name: Marktplatz market stalls
places.note: Grill stalls beside the Marienkapelle sell bratwurst in a roll to market shoppers.

places.name: Ratskeller Wuerzburg
places.note: Sit-down plates of bratwurst with kraut and potato salad in the town hall cellar.

places.name: Backoefele
places.note: Grilled over open fire in the old kitchen; a fixture of the menu for decades.

food.name: Fraenkisches Schaeufele
food.desc: Roast pork shoulder with the blade bone in, its crackling scored into a crisp lattice, served with potato dumplings and dark beer gravy.

places.name: Buergerspital Weinstuben
places.note: Traditional Sunday-lunch Schaeufele with Kloesse, matched to estate Silvaner.

places.name: Backoefele
places.note: Hearty, old-school portions in a room that has barely changed in decades.

places.name: Ratskeller Wuerzburg
places.note: Central and reliable for the full pork-and-dumpling Franconian plate.

food.name: Zwiebelkuchen
food.desc: Savoury onion and bacon tart baked in a tray, sold from late summer through the grape harvest and eaten with cloudy young Federweisser wine.

places.name: Weinhaus zum Stachel
places.note: Courtyard tavern that leans hard into the autumn Federweisser and Zwiebelkuchen season.

places.name: Juliusspital Weinstuben
places.note: Tavern of the 1576 hospital wine estate; seasonal tart with its own new wine.

places.name: Alte Mainmuehle
places.note: Riverside terrace where the autumn tart is eaten standing up with a Schoppen.

food.name: Fraenkische Brotzeit
food.desc: Cold wine-tavern board of Pressack head cheese, smoked ham, radish, spring onion, Obatzda cheese spread and pretzel or dark rye.

places.name: Juliusspital Weinstuben
places.note: Vesper boards designed to be eaten slowly with a flight of Franconian whites.

places.name: Buergerspital Weinstuben
places.note: Cool courtyard under vines; the Brotzeit plate is the light option here.

places.name: Weinhaus zum Stachel
places.note: Historic tavern where a board and a Bocksbeutel is a perfectly proper meal.

food.name: Frankenwein in Bocksbeutel
food.desc: Dry, mineral Silvaner and Mueller-Thurgau from the steep Main valley slopes, bottled in the region's squat flat-sided Bocksbeutel.

places.name: Staatlicher Hofkeller Wuerzburg
places.note: State wine cellar beneath the baroque Residenz palace; cellar tours and tastings.

places.name: Buergerspital Weinstuben
places.note: One of the world's oldest wine estates, pouring its own Silvaner by the Schoppen.

places.name: Juliusspital Weinstuben
places.note: The other great charitable estate; excellent dry Silvaner and Riesling by the glass.

food.name: Brueckenschoppen
food.desc: Not a wine but a ritual: a quarter-litre glass of Franconian white drunk standing on the Alte Mainbruecke at sunset, facing the fortress.

places.name: Alte Mainmuehle
places.note: The bridge hatch that started the tradition; buy a glass and take it onto the stonework.

places.name: Weinstuben on the Alte Mainbruecke
places.note: Several estate outlets sell by the glass at the bridge ends from spring to autumn.

places.name: Weinhaus zum Stachel
places.note: Two minutes from the bridge if the weather turns; same wines, seated in the courtyard.

landmarks: Würzburg Residence
A UNESCO-listed Baroque palace by Balthasar Neumann, crowned by Tiepolo's vast staircase fresco—the largest ceiling painting ever created in one piece.
Marienberg Fortress
This hilltop fortress guarded prince-bishops for centuries; its ramparts deliver postcard views over vineyards, the Main River and the old town's spires.
Old Main Bridge (Alte Mainbrücke)
Sip a glass of Franconian wine among Baroque saint statues on this pedestrian bridge, Würzburg's beloved sunset gathering spot since the 1730s.
Würzburg Cathedral (Dom St. Kilian)
One of Germany's largest Romanesque cathedrals, dedicated to the Irish missionary Kilian, blending medieval austerity with striking postwar modern art.
Marienkapelle
A late-Gothic market church in radiant red and white, adorned with replicas of Tilman Riemenschneider's famous Adam and Eve carvings.
Käppele
Balthasar Neumann's twin-onion-domed pilgrimage chapel gazes across the river at Marienberg Fortress, reached by a scenic stations-of-the-cross stairway.
Hofgarten (Residence Court Gardens)
Immaculate Baroque parterres, playful cherub statues and wrought-iron gates wrap around the Residence, offering a free and fragrant stroll behind the palace.
Neumünster
This Baroque-fronted Romanesque basilica rises over the grave of St. Kilian and shelters a serene courtyard linked to medieval poet Walther von der Vogelweide.
Falkenhaus
The city's most exuberant Rococo facade, a froth of yellow stucco on the Market Square now housing the tourist office and city library.
Alter Kranen (Old Crane)
An 18th-century twin-jib harbor crane on the Main riverbank, today the centerpiece of Würzburg's convivial riverside wine-drinking promenade.

train.note: Würzburg Hbf sits on the fast north-south ICE line, with Frankfurt about 70 minutes away, Munich 2 hours and Berlin 4. The ÖBB Railjet to Vienna passes through, which is the one direct international service. It is also the northern gateway to the Romantic Road. DB Sparpreis fares open six months ahead.

bus.note: Coaches stop at the Busbahnhof beside the Hauptbahnhof. FlixBus is effectively the only long-distance operator, running to Frankfurt, Munich, Nuremberg and onward into Czechia and Austria. The Romantic Road coach that once linked Würzburg with Rothenburg and Füssen no longer runs, so use regional trains and buses for that route.

ferry.note: There is no scheduled passenger ferry. Würzburg sits on the Main, where river cruise ships call and local excursion boats run in summer, but these are sightseeing rather than transport. A small ferry crosses to the Marienberg side seasonally.

half.name: Rothenburg ob der Tauber
half.blurb: Walled medieval town on the Romantic Road with half-timbered houses and intact fortifications.

half.name: Bamberg
half.blurb: UNESCO-listed old town built on seven hills, known for its cathedral and smoked beer breweries.

half.name: Nuremberg
half.blurb: Bavarian city with a medieval castle, old town squares, and Nazi-era historical sites.

half.name: Veitshöchheim
half.blurb: Small town with a Rococo summer palace and one of Europe's largest surviving 18th-century garden sculpture collections.
